reads.title: Charge
reads.text:
Charge

Generators bank charge from practice, notes and live goal completion according to their profiles, even in inventory. Deploy them beside receivers to deliver that supply while the board runs. Charge pauses between sessions; remaining reserves follow generators when moved.

Illustrative example — not your live board
Receiver A
strength 2
←
Generator
strength 2
→
Receiver B
strength 2

A and B each touch the generator. Each receives the full strength 2, not half. A distant receiver with no connection receives none.

Direct delivery reaches eligible adjacent receivers, not the whole board. Strengths from active generators add at a receiver. A generator spends reserve at its emission rate, not once per receiver; adding a neighbor does not shorten its remaining duration.

Oscillators and boosters use received charge continuously; a Module Forge accumulates it toward drafts. Each module’s profile and current readouts show its actual response. Conduits route received charge onward rather than generating it.

Decision: place supply beside the receivers you want to power. Check remaining reserve and received strength before moving a generator: ownership earns charge, but placement determines delivery. Current effects and prices stay on the live inspection and purchase surfaces.

reads.title: Chords and harmonic capacity
reads.text:
Chords and harmonic capacity

Recognition finds named pitch sets in connected voices, including silent voices. Adjacency alone is not a chord. Activation is a separate choice made automatically: only selected whole chords earn their member oscillators a bonus.

Illustrative example — not your live board

Suppose two recognized chords share a voice with capacity 1. Each chord needs one unit on every member. Both cannot activate together: selecting one leaves the other idle, even if its other members have spare capacity. No partial chord earns a bonus.

With capacity 2 on the shared voice, both can fit if every other member also has room. Fitting is not a promise of activation: the allocator chooses the set giving the highest total board production, and can leave chords idle when activating would reduce it.

Each voice has its type’s intrinsic capacity plus purchased Poly Expander increments. Silent voices also spend capacity. The purchase ceiling limits the purchased ladder, not a voice’s intrinsic seats. Active overlapping instances stack multiplicatively on their members; distant oscillators do not receive their bonus.

Diagnose an idle chord: open a participating hex and read Chord facts: its actual used/available capacity, active and idle names, factors and Formation read. Inspect the other members too: spare room on one voice does not establish room on all. Idle means recognized but unselected, not necessarily broken adjacency or insufficient capacity. The allocator compares final production, including charge and other effects; equal-output choices retain the previous active set before stable ordering.

The Catalog shows the actual next capacity price, allowance and ceiling. Use those live facts before buying or rearranging. These examples do not describe your current allocation.

Charge

reads.title: Prestige
reads.text:
Prestige

Prestige starts a new era while keeping your enduring progress. It banks the whole Arete in your pending claim. Arete buys memorized upgrades that survive later resets; repeating an old depth does not earn that claim again.

Illustrative example — not your live claim

If your pending claim is 3.4 Arete, prestige banks 3. The fraction stays pending. A later era must push beyond the frontier already claimed to build a new claim; merely reaching reset eligibility does not guarantee Arete.

Reaching the horizon makes reset eligible between sessions. A zero-yield reset is allowed, but banks no Arete. Nous, module levels, capacity purchases and charge state reset. Owned modules, cells and placement, memorized purchases, earned ordinary drafts and your life record remain.

Decision: compare the actual pending yield with the rebuild you are choosing. Check Reset era’s confirmation for this reset’s losses, preservation and warnings. Reading this page never resets your era or spends anything.

Charge

confirmation.text:

✕

About prestige

This prestige banks no Arete (0 Arete) and starts the era over: module levels return to base, purchased capacity returns to one, and your nous and charge return to the opening.

Your board and its placement, the tray, banked Forge rolls and progress, feats, your whole life record, your Arete, your scrap, and lifetime nous all stay — as do your World columns, weapons, and 
Hone
 ranks.

Not yet
Prestige anyway
